item.text: {"question_id":"6B.10","answer":"The evidence does not establish that ordinary people finished 2023 with durably better life chances than inherited. There were genuine, ruler-period institutional measures: Bürgergeld raised support and expanded training-oriented assistance; Wohngeld Plus was intended to broaden housing support; BAföG spending and average awards increased slightly in coverage and substantially in amount; care legislation promised benefit and system improvements; and modeled analysis found that social transfers, energy support and gas-market stabilization protected lower-income consumption more than higher-income consumption (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0034-R12-E004). Some outcome indicators were favorable but qualified: child poverty risk declined from 15.0% to 14.0%, and modeled 2023 effective-wage gains were strongest in the lowest quintile. However, the child-poverty income measure principally reflects 2022 income, the series is affected by EU-SILC redesign and lacks comparable pre-2020 trends; the wage and inequality findings are nowcasts, and the lower-quintile gains were linked partly to the inherited October 2022 minimum-wage increase and inflation-compensation payments, while cumulative real-wage losses remained unrecovered (BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0035-E007). End-period conditions remained materially unequal and insecure: 17.7 million people were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, including 23.9% of children, with a 36.8% poverty risk among children whose parents had low educational qualifications; care needs rose amid demographic and definitional effects; housing approvals fell sharply; and unemployment and underemployment increased even as social-insurance employment growth came entirely from foreign employment (BATCH-0023-E012; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0022-E009; BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0009-E021). Disadvantaged groups faced persistent barriers: refugee integration showed a large gender employment gap, qualification-recognition and residence-policy constraints, and childcare shortages of about 430,000 places; reception capacity was severely strained, with overcrowding, inadequate sanitation and health-care access, registration backlogs and limited privacy in reported locations (BATCH-0011-R06-E009; BATCH-0011-R06-E010; BATCH-0011-R06-E011; BATCH-0011-R04-E014). The Ukraine protection regime and access to social protection were consequential institutional supports, but the cited population and legal-access evidence does not itself demonstrate improved or durable realized life chances (BATCH-0008-E004). Attribution is institutional and partial rather than personal: federal measures occurred under Scholz, while implementation depended substantially on Länder and municipalities; outcomes also reflect the energy and inflation shock, Russia’s war, monetary and labor-market conditions, demographic change, donor or external roles where applicable, inherited measures and policy lags. Durability beyond 2023, broad service quality, regional variation and several disadvantaged-group outcomes remain insufficiently demonstrated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0035-E007","BATCH-0008-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E012","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0022-E009","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0009-E021","BATCH-0025-E016","BATCH-0011-R06-E009","BATCH-0011-R06-E010","BATCH-0011-R06-E011","BATCH-0011-R04-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most poverty-risk income measures principally reflect prior-year income; some are first results, and EU-SILC redesign prevents direct comparison with pre-2020 years.","The wage and inequality evidence includes modeled or provisional estimates and does not establish durable post-2023 gains.","Durability beyond 2023 is not demonstrated.","Several policy sources describe design or intended effects without independent evidence of take-up, incidence, service quality or realized outcomes.","Attribution is generally to federal institutions during Scholz's period, not to Scholz personally; Länder, municipalities, inherited policies, external shocks, demographic change and monetary conditions also matter.","Evidence remains limited or uneven for housing quality, water and sanitation outside reception settings, regional inequality, and broad disadvantaged-group life chances; reception-condition evidence is not a nationally standardized inspection.","Refugee labor-market findings concern earlier cohorts and do not cleanly isolate beneficiaries of protection or policies enacted in 2023."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed the implication that 2023 poverty-risk results are contemporaneous, fully attributable end-period outcomes.","Downgraded positive weight for child-poverty, BAföG and low-quintile wage evidence by incorporating prior-year income, methodological breaks, inherited minimum-wage effects, modeled nowcasts and unrecovered cumulative real-wage losses.","Added refugee employment and gender-gap evidence, childcare shortage evidence, and care-system pressure.","Reframed Ukraine temporary protection as institutional access rather than demonstrated durable life-chance improvement.","Separated federal institutional attribution from personal Scholz attribution and from Länder, municipal, inherited-policy and shock effects."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be warranted if final comparable post-2023 outcomes, policy-incidence studies, regional and subgroup data, or independent evaluations of Bürgergeld, Wohngeld Plus, BAföG, care reforms and refugee integration become available.","The evidence base should be reopened to test durability and to distinguish inherited baseline trends, delayed policy effects and external shocks from ruler-attributable changes."]}
